title: America's 7th Biggest Company Was a Lie #shorts
description:
In 2001, Enron was one of the most admired companies in America. Within weeks it was bankrupt, and its stock went from about $90 to almost nothing.
Hidden debt, fake profits, and the fall of a giant.
Follow for more stories of money that vanished overnight.
hook_text:
FROM $90 A SHARE
TO ALMOST NOTHING
first_comment: Who failed worse here: the executives, or the auditors who signed off on it? 👇

lines.text: In two thousand, Enron was the seventh biggest company in America.
A year later, it was gone.
Magazines called it the most innovative company in the country, six years in a row.
Its stock hit about ninety dollars a share.
But the profits were not what they seemed.
Billions in debt were hidden inside secret side companies, off the books.
In October two thousand and one, the truth started to leak out.
The stock collapsed to less than one dollar.
In December, Enron filed for bankruptcy, the largest in American history at the time.
About twenty thousand people lost their jobs. Many lost their savings too.
Its top executives were convicted, and its auditor, Arthur Andersen, collapsed with it.
Follow for more stories of money that vanished overnight.
